title: bug: release_task without force treats an explicit blank/null workerId as human and releases a live peer between steps
description:
Found during task-0adea941 QA repair self-review. The proxy injects only absent workerId keys; without force, releaseTask.ts reaches claimGuards.assertReleaseCaller's `if (!caller) return`, so explicit '' or null releases a peer-held row with no IN_PROGRESS step.
Snapshot /tmp/moe-0adea941-red-BP1LVK contains the repaired force gates plus a scratch '(follow-up)' test in src/tools/releaseForceGate.test.ts: npx vitest run src/tools/releaseForceGate.test.ts -t follow-up (env -i) passed 2 probes proving success:true and task-idle assignee null. Log: packages/nonforce-repro.log.
Keep this separate from the approved force-only contract: preserve genuine omitted-ID human/board recovery and legitimate own-row releases, refuse malformed supplied IDs before writes, and correct docs/MCP_SERVER.md:2030's stale 'Anyone can call — no ownership check' claim.
definitionOfDone: Without force, explicit blank/null/non-string caller IDs cannot release a peer-held row between steps and refusal writes nothing.
Absent-ID human/board recovery, valid own-row release, and governor/human force controls remain green.
release_task documentation accurately describes its ownership checks rather than saying there are none.

implementationPlan.note: Appended (n1) it.each over 8 malformed callers, (n2), (n3) to releaseForceGate.test.ts. RED-at-base is run in step 3.

Added the workerId shape guard after the force gate in releaseTask.ts, replaced the 'Anyone can call' sentence in the tool description, and rewrote the release_task ownership paragraph in docs/MCP_SERVER.md.

implementationPlan.description:
Adversarial self-review of your `git diff`. Fix any finding, re-run step 3, then call complete_task.
(1) Scope:
- releaseTask.ts gains only the guard and the description sentence.
- MCP_SERVER.md changes only the release_task paragraph.
- releaseForceGate.test.ts gains only (n1) to (n3).
- claimGuards.ts is untouched.
(2) Ordering: force plus a malformed id is still refused NOT_ALLOWED by the 0adea941 gate, so (p7) is green. No force plus a malformed id is INVALID_INPUT. Both are thrown before handoff capture and before the mutex.
(3) Who still releases:
- an omitted workerId: the board, a human, moe-call.sh without MOE_WORKER_ID, the DONE/ARCHIVED no-op and the unassigned repair;
- the holder's own id, even mid-step;
- a governor or omitted id with force.
A well-formed non-holder id is still RELEASE_NOT_ASSIGNEE (n3), or STEP_LEASE_HELD mid-step.
(4) A whitespace-padded real id such as ' worker-1 ' is not blank, so it passes the guard and is judged as an id: not the holder, so it is refused. That matches today's behaviour for any non-holder string.
(5) Concurrency: the guard reads only the call's own arguments, so there is no race. Would you be embarrassed if `workerId: ""` still stripped a peer? (n1)'s spies prove it cannot even read the task.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: Without force, moe.release_task treats only an OMITTED workerId as the human/board path. A supplied workerId that is blank, whitespace-only or not a string ('', null, 0, false, 123, {}, []) is refused with INVALID_INPUT before any read or write. Such an id can no longer release a row a peer holds between steps, as it could via assertReleaseCaller's falsy-caller skip. Omitted-id human/board releases, a holder's own release, a well-formed non-holder's RELEASE_NOT_ASSIGNEE/STEP_LEASE_HELD refusals and 0adea941's governor/human force gate are unchanged. The tool description and docs/MCP_SERVER.md describe these ownership checks instead of 'Anyone can call — no ownership check'.
acceptanceCriteria: (n1) For each of 8 malformed workerId values, a release without force of task-idle (held by worker-peer2 between steps), task-peer (mid-step) or a missing task is refused with codeName INVALID_INPUT. getTask, runExclusive, touchWorker and appendActivity are never called, and tasks, workers and resources are unchanged.
(n2) An omitted workerId releases task-idle between steps (previousWorkerId worker-peer2), and the holder worker-peer releases its own mid-step task-peer.
(n3) A well-formed non-holder (worker-1) is still refused RELEASE_NOT_ASSIGNEE on task-idle, and the row is unchanged.
The existing force-gate cases (p1) to (p7) and (r1) to (r5) and every other release_task-driving suite pass: 15 files, 513 tests.
docs/MCP_SERVER.md's release_task section no longer says 'no ownership check' and contains 'before anything is read or written: the proxy injects'.
invariants: An omitted workerId behaves exactly as before.
force plus a malformed id is still refused NOT_ALLOWED by the force gate, which runs first.
A refusal writes nothing and takes no lock.
compatibility: The board (WebSocketServer RELEASE_TASK) and the wrappers' launch_outage_release keep working: they omit workerId or send a real one.
No schema or record-shape change: workerId stays an optional string, and only malformed values are newly refused.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Three fixes were weighed.
(1) Chosen: one boundary guard in releaseTask.ts. A supplied workerId that is not a non-blank string is refused INVALID_INPUT before any read or write. This matches the row's "refuse malformed supplied IDs before writes" and the key-presence rule 0adea941 uses (setTaskStatus.ts:105 style): only an absent key is the human/board path.
(2) Rejected: changing claimGuards.assertReleaseCaller to judge '' as a non-holder (RELEASE_NOT_ASSIGNEE). That still lets a malformed id repair an unassigned row and write a non-string `releasedBy`/actor into the handoff and activity log. It also leaves 123/{} refused with odd 'not [object Object]' text.
(3) Rejected: refusing every non-holder on unassigned rows. That breaks the documented recovery and repair paths.
The refusal code is INVALID_INPUT rather than NOT_ALLOWED: the input is malformed, nobody is denied a permission. The force path keeps 0adea941's NOT_ALLOWED.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
assertReleaseCaller's `if (!caller) return` (claimGuards.ts:294) is the hole: '', null, 0 and false skip the holder check. Truthy non-strings were already refused, but as RELEASE_NOT_ASSIGNEE.
assertNoLiveLease still protects mid-step rows from every non-holder, so the observable bug is limited to rows between steps (task-idle).
The board's RELEASE_TASK omits workerId, and the wrappers' launch_outage_release always sends WORKER_ID.
The daemon snapshot gate needs `scripts` archived for delivery/acceptance.test.ts, which spawns the real moe-agent.sh. Without it the test exits 127 at base too.
Architect dry run at 395172f0:
- RED: 8 failed | 36 passed (44);
- GREEN: 15 files, 513/513, tsc clean;
- both checkRefs passed verbatim, uncommitted and after a simulated landing.
